title: Understanding SVD Dimensions
text: When performing Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) on a matrix X with dimensions $$n$$ by $$d$$, the resulting matrices U, S, and $$V^T$$ have specific dimensions. Consider how the dimensions of U and $$V^T$$ relate to the original matrix X.

title: Rank and Dimensions
text: Remember that the rank of a matrix is the maximum number of linearly independent column vectors in the matrix. How does the rank of X, which is less than $$d$$, affect the dimensions of the matrices in the SVD?

title: Dimensions of U and $$V^T$$
text: Given that X is an $$n$$ by $$d$$ matrix, what are the possible dimensions of U and $$V^T$$?
